Context: this is one page of a numbered list of 'Lambert-series' evaluations of theta products (the '(1.xy)' list). The next page repeats (1.81)-(1.84) as (3.31)-(3.34) and introduces them as cases where 'the partition method gives the actual value'. Notation: q = x, psi(q) = sum_{n>=0} q^{n(n+1)/2} = 1+q+q^3+q^6+..., chi_d(n) = Kronecker symbol (d/n), sigma_k(n) = sum of k-th powers of the divisors of n.

(1.72) The left side is x*psi(x)*psi(x^7), since 1+x^7+x^21+x^42+... = psi(x^7). The right side is the Lambert series over odd n of (n/7) x^n/(1-x^n). The printed signs at n = 1,3,5,9,11,13,15,17 are +,-,-,+,+,-,+,- and n = 7 is omitted. This is exactly (n/7) for odd n.
- In coefficient form: #{(a,b) : a(a+1)/2 + 7b(b+1)/2 = N-1} = sum_{d|N, d odd} (d/7).
- [mine] Because (2/7) = +1, this equals sum_{n>=1} (n/7) q^n/(1-q^{2n}), the usual modern form.

(1.81) a(q) := sum_{m,n in Z} q^{m^2+mn+n^2} = 1 + 6 sum_{n>=1} (n/3) q^n/(1-q^n). Equivalently r(N) = 6 sum_{d|N} (d/3), with signs +,-,+,- at n = 1,2,4,5.

(1.82) a(q)^2 = 1 + 12 sum_{3 does not divide n} n q^n/(1-q^n). [mine] This equals 1 + 12 sum sigma(N) q^N - 36 sum sigma(N) q^{3N}. Since M_2(Gamma_0(3)) is 1-dimensional, it equals (3E_2(q^3) - E_2(q))/2.

(1.83) a(q)^3 = 1 - 9 sum (n/3) n^2 q^n/(1-q^n) + 27 sum n^2 q^n/(1+q^n+q^{2n}).
- [mine] q^n/(1+q^n+q^{2n}) = q^n(1-q^n)/(1-q^{3n}) = sum_k (k/3) q^{nk}.
- So the coefficient of q^N is -9 sum_{d|N} (d/3) d^2 + 27 sum_{d|N} (N/d over 3) d^2.
- These are the two weight-3 Eisenstein series of level 3 with character chi_{-3}.

(1.84) a(q)^4 = 1 + 24 sum n^3 q^n/(1-q^n) + 8 sum (3n)^3 q^{3n}/(1-q^{3n}). That is, coefficient(N) = 24 sigma_3(N) + 216 sigma_3(N/3). [mine] This equals (E_4(q) + 9E_4(q^3))/10.

(1.91) T(q) := sum q^{m^2+mn+2n^2} (discriminant -7, class number 1) = 1 + 2 sum (n/7) q^n/(1-q^n). The printed signs at n = 1..10 are +,+,-,+,-,-,(0),+,+,-, which match (n/7). Hence r(N) = 2 sum_{d|N} (d/7).

(1.92) T(q)^2 = 1 + 4 sum_{7 does not divide n} n q^n/(1-q^n). The printed list 1,2,3,4,5,6,8 skips 7. [mine] This equals 1 + 4 sum sigma(N) q^N - 28 sum sigma(N) q^{7N} = (7E_2(q^7) - E_2(q))/6, since M_2(Gamma_0(7)) is 1-dimensional.

Purpose: these are a catalogue of exact formulas for the number of representations by the forms m^2+mn+n^2 and m^2+mn+2n^2 (and their 2nd-4th powers), and by triangular numbers with weights 1,7. In each case the modular-form space is spanned by Eisenstein series, so the singular-series ('partition method') expression is exact.

[my spot checks] Low-order coefficients agree:
- a = 1+6q+0q^2+6q^3+6q^4+...
- a^2: q^1 coefficient 12, q^2 coefficient 36.
- a^3: q coefficient 18 = -9+27; q^2 coefficient 108 = 27+81.
- a^4: q coefficient 24.
- T = 1+2q+4q^2+0q^3+...
- T^2: q coefficient 4, q^2 coefficient 12.
- x psi(x) psi(x^7) = x+x^2+x^4+x^7+x^8+x^9+2x^11+..., matching sum_{d odd, d|N} (d/7).
errors: No mathematical errors found; all seven identities are correct as written, including the sign patterns (Legendre symbols mod 3 and mod 7) and the omission of terms with 3|n or 7|n where required.
(1.72) RHS runs only over odd n; this is correct and equivalent to the more common sum_n (n/7) q^n/(1-q^{2n}) because (2/7)=1. This equivalence is not stated on the page.
Proofs are not given on this page; the formulas are stated without derivation (presumably to be justified by the 'partition method' of the surrounding manuscript).

results.modern_name: Lambert series for psi(q)psi(q^7); representations of N as T_a + 7T_b (triangular numbers)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (notebooks, Chapter 17/19 entries, proved in Berndt, Ramanujan's Notebooks Part III)

results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet/Lorenz (1871); Ramanujan notebooks; Borweins (1991) for the cubic theory

results.modern_name: weight-2 Eisenstein series on Gamma_0(3); representations by sums of two copies of the hexagonal form
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (notebooks / this manuscript); Lorenz-type results; standard modular forms theory

results.modern_name: weight-3 Eisenstein series with character chi_{-3} on Gamma_0(3)
results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (lost notebook/manuscripts; discussed by Berndt, Andrews-Berndt)

results.usually_credited_to: Ramanujan (manuscripts); standard theory of modular forms

results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (19th c.) via class number one; Ramanujan notebooks

deep.surprise_reason: These are exactly the Eisenstein-series identities for the hexagonal and discriminant -7 forms that Ramanujan is known to have recorded (notebooks, and this partition-method manuscript, which is discussed in the Andrews-Berndt lost-notebook volumes). They are correct and elegant but well documented as his.
